report.source_text: The initial ophthalmic examination demonstrated a best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 6/6 in the right eye and counting fingers (CF) at a distance of 0.5 feet in the left eye. Intraocular pressure was recorded at 12 mmHg in both eyes. Examination of the left eye revealed a relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD). The patient displayed full extraocular movements in both eyes. Anterior segment evaluation of the left eye was unremarkable.

report.source_text: Investigations for congenital and acquired thrombophilia, such as prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), international normalized ratio (INR), antiphospholipid antibodies, and factor V Leiden mutation yielded normal results. The patient also did not have other common risk factors such as diabetes, hyperlipidemia, or autoimmune conditions. Her autoimmune profile was normal. No plaque or thrombus was noted on carotid Doppler ultrasonography. Echocardiography was also unremarkable. Abdominal and pelvic ultrasound reports were unremarkable.

report.source_text: However, dilated fundus examination revealed findings indicative of central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO), including optic disc edema, 360 degrees of preretinal hemorrhages, venous dilation and tortuosity, and cotton wool spots. Furthermore, a white ischemic area was observed nasally to the fovea, suggestive of a possible ciliary retinal artery occlusion (Fig. 1).

report.source_text: At 6 weeks, after resolution of the preretinal hemorrhages, panretinal photocoagulation was performed to prevent neovascular glaucoma, which is associated with central retinal vein occlusion within 90 days. It was performed prophylactically as the patient resides in a remote area and was unwilling to adhere to a regular follow-up schedule.
